Protein Synthesis
Production of protein 
one of the major functions of the cell
General process from synthesis to export:
Proteins assembled by ribosomes on the rough ER
Vesicles transportproteins to the Golgi
Proteins are modifiedby the Golgi and enter newvesicles
Some vesicles release proteins outside the cell (cell signaling, hormones, etc.)
Some vesicles remain in the cell and become lysosomes, peroxisomes, etc.
Processes like this that use these organelles known as Endomembrane System
explanation: Protein synthesis and export represent one of the major functions of a cell. The general pathway proceeds as follows: proteins are first assembled by ribosomes bound to the Rough ER; next, vesicles transport these newly synthesized proteins to the Golgi apparatus; the Golgi modifies the proteins and packages them into new vesicles. From there, some vesicles migrate to the plasma membrane and release their contents outside the cell (such as hormones or signaling molecules), while other vesicles remain inside the cell to function as lysosomes, peroxisomes, or other organelles. This interconnected pathway of organelles and vesicles is known collectively as the Endomembrane System.

questions.q: What is the correct pathway of a secretory protein through the endomembrane system?
opts: Ribosome on Rough ER -> Vesicle -> Golgi -> Vesicle -> Destination (inside or outside cell)
questions.exp: As described in the slide, proteins are assembled by ribosomes on the rough ER, transported by vesicles to the Golgi, modified by the Golgi, and then packaged into new vesicles for export or internal use.
